title: Ladder cost: $294k vs $298.6k on the same 15 Oct curve; which figure for which claim
problem: On the 15 Oct curve, Caplet's files give 'about $294,000, $5,500 headroom' (number sheet) and '$298,624, $1,376' (lenses). Both are right, but they answer different questions. $294k (payment dates, forward basis) assumes the money from each bond earns today's implied rates in a short-term Treasury fund until the 1 Jan payment, which is what the team's notes say happens. $298.6k (owned maturity dates, curve unchanged) assumes that money earns nothing in the gap, so it is a cautious upper bound. A reader sees opposite stories ('comfortable room' or 'almost none'). The number sheet's '1 case in 3' belongs to the $294k basis only. The room also moves fast: 14 to 15 Oct it fell from $8,242 to $5,539 (payment-date basis) and from $4,007 to $1,372 (owned, unchanged).

title: Names a bond judge reads differently: 'Caplet', 'cap', 'floor', 'root-and-branch'
problem: To a fixed-income reader a caplet is one period of an interest-rate cap (an option, a derivative, and WInS bans derivatives), and 'cap' and 'floor' are names of interest-rate derivatives.
